prompts: Fix normalize(response) in evidence.py. A response has retrieved documents with id/url and explicit cited_ids in answer order. Return retrieved_sources with unique retrieved documents in first-seen order, and cited_sources with only documents named by cited_ids in citation order, deduplicated. Reject a cited ID absent from retrieval with ValueError rather than fabricating a source. Do not count every retrieved document as a citation.

checks.name: separate-evidence-semantics
command:
from evidence import normalize
docs=[{'id':'a','url':'https://a.example.invalid'},{'id':'b','url':'https://b.example.invalid'},{'id':'c','url':'https://c.example.invalid'}]
r=normalize({'retrieved':docs+[dict(docs[0])],'cited_ids':['c','a','c']})
assert r['retrieved_sources']==docs and r['cited_sources']==[docs[2],docs[0]]
assert normalize({'retrieved':docs,'cited_ids':[]})['cited_sources']==[]
try:normalize({'retrieved':docs,'cited_ids':['unknown']})
except ValueError:pass
else:raise AssertionError('Unknown citation invented')

rubric: Preserve the distinct semantics and provenance of retrieved context and actual answer citations. Never promote all retrieval to citation evidence or invent a missing source. Keep ordering and deduplication contracts without creating a second parallel source-of-truth representation.
provenance: codex-20-retrieval-context-and-citations-have-different-semantics; sanitized incident reconstruction; no historical pre-error workspace recovered.
